chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ibn Najiya, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba, from Najiya. He said: Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said:
When you pray Asr on Friday, then say:

'O Allah! Bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the deputies (awsiya) whom Allah is pleased with, with the best of Your blessings. Send benedictions to them with the best of Your benedictions. Peace be upon them, their spirits, their bodies, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.'

For whoever says this after Asr, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, records one hundred thousand good deeds for him, erases one hundred thousand sins from him, fulfills one hundred thousand needs for him, and raises him by one hundred thousand degrees.

key_terms.الأوصياء: The deputies/successors — refers to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt as divinely-appointed successors to the Prophet
key_terms.الحسنة: Good deed — a meritorious act recorded by the angels
key_terms.الدرجة: Degree/rank — spiritual elevation in the sight of Allah
key_terms.السيئة: Sin/evil deed — a transgression recorded against one's account
key_terms.الصلوات: Blessings/salawat — invocations of divine blessing upon the Prophet and his family
key_terms.المرضيين: The well-pleasing ones — those with whom Allah is pleased; an honorific for the Imams

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited after Asr prayer on Friday according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him), the fifth Imam, teaches a specific supplication to be recited after the Asr prayer on Fridays, invoking blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad and his blessed family, the awsiya (divinely-appointed successors). The supplication holds enormous spiritual rewards: one hundred thousand good deeds recorded, one hundred thousand sins erased, one hundred thousand needs fulfilled, and one hundred thousand degrees of spiritual elevation. In early Islamic scholarly tradition, Friday Asr was regarded as a particularly blessed time for du'a and salawat, and this narration reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the spiritual role of the Ahl al-Bayt as awsiya (deputies/successors).

al-Baqir (the one who splits knowledge open)
the well-pleasing (those with whom Allah is pleased)

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Muhammad b. `Isa b. `Ubayd al-Yaqtini from Zakariyya al-Mu’min from Ibn Najiya from Dawud b. al-Nu`man from `Abd al-Rahman b. Siyaba from Najiya. He said: Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (as) said:
When you pray `Asr on Friday, then say:

“O Allah! Bless Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, the deputies whom Allah is pleased with, with the best of Your blessings. Send benedictions to them with the best of Your benedictions. Peace be with them, their spirits, their bodies, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings (Allahumma salli `ala Muhammadin wa aali Muhammad al-awsiya al-murdiyyin bi afdal salawatik, wa baarik `alayhum bi afdal barakatik, wassalaam `alayhum wa `ala arwahuhum wa ajsaduhum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh).”

Whoever says this after `Asr, Allah records one hundred thousand good deeds for him, erases one hundred thousand sins from him, fulfills one hundred thousand needs for him, and raises him by one hundred thousand degrees.
